title: WMI shadow-copy deletion: capability vs observed command

claims.text: LockBit 2.0 can use wmic.exe to delete volume shadow copies.
cmd.exe /c wmic SHADOWCOPY /nointeractive — the FBI's recorded description is "This command has an invalid syntax and errors out."
claims.locator: FBI Flash CU-000162-MW · Command Line Activity

interpretation: A capability mapping from vendor analysis and a single field-observed command can both be true. The observed command failed in that sample; do not assume every wmic shadow-copy deletion attempt succeeds.
analystAction: Validate the command variant in the environment and keep alternative recovery-inhibition paths (vssadmin, bcdedit, PowerShell) in scope.

title: Log destruction mapped two ways

claims.text: Data Destruction — LockBit 3.0 deletes log files and empties the recycle bin.
Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs — LockBit executable clears the Windows Event Logs files.

interpretation: The statements can describe different artifacts: Windows Event Logs versus general log files and the recycle bin. ATT&CK v20.0 uses T1685.005; the source’s T1070.001 is revoked. The source IDs are not interchangeable.
analystAction: Write separate detections for event log clearing, log-file deletion and recycle-bin destruction. Do not deduplicate them by a single TTP label.

title: Safe Mode: documented in March, absent from the June tables

claims.text: LockBit 3.0 has a Safe Mode feature to circumvent endpoint antivirus and detection.
claims.locator: CISA AA23-075A · Safe Mode Launch Commands

claims.text: Not listed in the June 2023 advisory's ATT&CK tables 5–16.

interpretation: This is a coverage difference, not a contradiction. The June advisory is broader and not exhaustive; the March advisory contains build-specific command-line detail. Absence from one table is not evidence the behaviour was removed.
analystAction: Keep the Safe Mode hypothesis active and treat the March advisory as the stronger source for this specific capability.
